gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-vai: Precise and modern, Blockletter has a tube-like thickness that holds through every bend, like a pencil that never presses harder. And Noto Sans Vai handles the quieter work, its words settling into solid blocks with generous room where curves meet the stem.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-wanc:
Noto Sans Wancho is hulking, like thick chalk pressed hard.

Blockletter above it keeps a flat, sign-painter's-stencil line, so the text below feels weighty and the e's wide terminal gap lets each word breathe as the paragraphs pile up.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-wara:
Blockletter draws its joints without any thinning or bulging.

Noto Sans Warang Citi follows with words that settle into solid blocks, and wide channels leading into each counter give the text a clean, contemporary footing under that precise, pencil-sketched heading.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-yi: Pencil-sketched and swing-free, Blockletter holds its strokes to a single thickness with a tall, squat-bellied midsection. But Noto Sans Yi sits underneath with a deep lowercase and rounds left unlatched, so the heading's rigor meets something more open.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-zana:
Approachable and contemporary, Noto Sans Zanabazar Square soars with a tall x-height while Blockletter looks drawn with a fixed pen.

Noto Sans Zanabazar Square keeps tiny sizes crisp thanks to wide gaps, and that crispness is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-numans:
Wire-thin strokes, all one thickness, and a squat brush-pen belly: that's Blockletter, precise and modern.

Numans answers with swollen, rope-coiled lowercase, an s whose ends hang far from the spine, and tracking pushed well past normal.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-onest: Precise, pencil-drawn Blockletter has a squat, tall-bellied shape that is made to be looked at. But Onest does the reading, with short ascenders above big bowls and a gentle monotone line that never pools where curves turn in.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-open-sans:
Open Sans reads smoothly, with no clogged curves and bulky lowercase proportions.

Open Sans carries a longer passage without friction, while Blockletter's rounded-nib strokes, free of swelling at the ends, hold the top of the page.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-orienta: Rounded-wire strokes with horizontals as thick as verticals: Blockletter looks precise and sketched. Orienta's counters breathe like a cut hollow reed, so nudge its size up a touch, since little height separates its cases.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-oxygen:
Oxygen reads cleanly, its curves never closing back on themselves and its lowercase nearly matching the capitals.
